prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” across all of Atlanta — the right company depends on your exact location, budget, home size, and priorities (price, speed, brand, warranty). I can find the top-rated installers near you and compare quotes if you share your ZIP code. 

Things that usually separate the best installers
- Proper sizing (Manual J load calculation) — not just “match the old unit.”
- NATE-certified technicians and a Georgia contractor’s license + insurance.
- Manufacturer certification for the brand they install (Trane/Carrier/Lennox/etc.), good warranties, and clear labor warranty terms.
- Written, itemized estimates (equipment, labor, permit, ductwork, disposal).
- Upfront answers about required permits, expected timeline, and any ductwork/airflow issues.
- Strong recent reviews (Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB) and local references.
- Energy-efficiency advice (SEER ratings), and explanation of operating cost tradeoffs.
- Financing options if you need them.

Typical process and tips
- Get 3 written bids from reputable companies in your area.
- Require a Manual J load calc and written explanation of recommended capacity.
- Check reviews and ask for 2–3 local references.
- Verify license/insurance and ask if they pull permits.
- Ask about brands they recommend and whether they’re factory-certified.
- Compare total installed cost and long-term value (efficiency + warranty).

Rough cost expectation (Atlanta area, residential central AC)
- Usually about $3,500–$8,500+ depending on size, SEER, brand, ductwork, and whether you need a new condenser + air handler/coil.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies in your ZIP and return 3–5 vetted options with review scores and phone numbers.
- Or build an email/phone script and checklist so you can quickly compare bids.

Which would you prefer? If you want me to search, please give your ZIP code and whether this is a house or commercial property.
